body:
Maya (PM): Quick sync notes — ran the mock with pool search + SLO slider together and a couple of issues popped up. Attaching screenshot: https://files.redwood/mock-pool-search.png. Need quick takes on ranking, copy, and accessibility before we freeze the pattern.

Sam (Design): Saw it. Main thing: search results feel noisy when min/max is shown inline. Users scan for GPU type first, not capacity. Suggest moving min/max under a collapsible "capacity" row and surface a small badge for "burst available" next to pool name.

Jun (Eng): Collapsible rows add complexity but doable. Backend can return a "burst_available" flag in the pool search response. API sketch: `GET /pools?q=...&include_burst=true` -> pool.burst_available boolean. Will cost a little extra DB join, but fine.

Ellie (Frontend): Agree with Sam. Also keyboarding is broken when the capacity row expands — focus jumps to the wrong element. We should ensure arrow keys keep focus within results and `Enter` opens details. I can add `role="listbox"` + `aria-activedescendant` pattern.

Kai (Accessibility): Important: when the SLO slider updates predicted throughput we must announce the new value via `aria-live="polite"`. Also color alone shouldn't communicate "soft cap" vs "hard cap" — add text like "Recommended max" vs "Hard limit" and high-contrast borders for the slider thumb at thresholds.

Sam (Design): On copy: replace "burst" with "Burst capacity" in labels, but keep the tiny badge text `+burst` to save space. For the slider tooltip, change "SLO" to "Target latency (ms)" on hover, with an inline hint: "Lower = faster, higher cost".

Maya (PM): Nice. One sticky: how do we surface when a pool is a recommended fallback (guardrail) vs user-configured? People confuse automatic fallback with their requested min.

Jun (Eng): We could add a small chevron `Recommended` badge and a dotted outline for recommended pools. The realtime allocator can tag pools with `recommended_reason`: e.g., `capacity`, `latency`, `cost`. We'll only show the badge when the reason is present.

Ellie (Frontend): Implementation note: use `data-reason` attribute and let CSS handle the dotted outline. For screenreader, include `aria-describedby` referencing a visually-hidden span: "Recommended fallback: preserves SLO during flux."

Kai (Accessibility): For the SLO slider, ensure keyboard step sizes are clear: `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax`, `aria-valuetext` like "Target latency 150ms — near recommended max". Also test with VoiceOver — sliders sometimes announce raw numbers, not context.

Sam (Design): Visual tweak idea: show a tiny sparkline under each pool result indicating recent SLO hit-rate (green/orange/red). If red, surface a warning: "This pool frequently triggers guardrail — may increase cost." Keeps the list scannable while adding signal.

Jun (Eng): Sparkline is fine client-side if we get a compact time-series sample (5 points). We'll cap at 5 to avoid payload bloat: `slo_samples: [0.98,0.95,0.67,0.45,0.32]`.

Maya (PM): Agree on 5-point series. Action items: Sam — update mocks with collapsible capacity row, `+burst` badge, sparkline and recommended badge. Jun — add `burst_available` flag + `slo_samples` and `recommended_reason` to search API. Ellie — keyboard/focus fixes + `aria-activedescendant` pattern. Kai — quick a11y pass on slider copy/announcements and screenreader notes. I'll follow up with a short draft PR for microcopy.

Ellie (Frontend): One more: when users change min/max from the pool picker, show an inline confirmation toast that includes the estimated cost delta (small number). That helps prevent accidental big commits.

Jun (Eng): Estimation service exists; I'll wire a `predicted_cost_delta` field for the selection preview.

Sam (Design): Microcopy proposal for the toast: "Updated min/max. Estimated cost change: +$12/day. Changes are effective immediately but can be reverted." Short and scannable.

Kai (Accessibility): Toasts should be `role="status"` and `aria-live="polite"` so screen readers announce the cost change. Also provide a keyboard-focusable "Undo" in the toast.

Maya (PM): Great. Timeline: Sam + Ellie — updated mocks by EOD Thurs, Jun + Kai — backend & a11y tweaks by end of week. I'll collate and book a quick 20-min sign-off on Friday. :thumbsup:
